title: Naturality of the scalar cohomology to Ext comparison
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, $F,G$ arbitrary $\mathcal O_X$-modules, and $\phi:F\to G$. For the recorded right-derived-functor scalar cohomology, scalar sheaf coefficient map $S_f(\phi)$, and comparison $e_{F,n}:H_k^n(X,F)\cong\operatorname{Ext}^n(\mathbf1,S_fF)$ [def-sc-field-linear-module-cohomology-operations], every $n\in\mathbb N$ and $a\in H_k^n(X,F)$ satisfy $e_{G,n}(H_k^n(\phi)(a))=e_{F,n}(a)\cdot\operatorname{Ext}^0(S_f(\phi))$. This compares a single coefficient morphism and involves neither cup products nor scheme pullbacks.

source.place: Cohomology Tags 01DZ and 01F7, injective-resolution comparison and coefficient functoriality. Official text read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01F7 and the indicated tag pages.

proof.text: Lift a coefficient morphism to a comparison map of injective resolutions. The right-derived-functor coefficient map is induced by the global-sections map of this comparison. Evaluation at 1 identifies the global-sections complex with Hom from the structure sheaf, naturally in the resolution: every O-linear comparison map takes the image of 1 to the image of the corresponding section. The cocycle formula specifying moduleExtEquiv therefore intertwines the derived coefficient map with postcomposition by the degree-zero Ext class of the coefficient morphism. Every cohomology class has a cocycle representative, so this proves naturality of moduleExtEquiv. Exact restriction to scalar sheaves preserves Yoneda composition and sends the degree-zero coefficient map to scalarHom. Precompose by scalarUnitMorphism and use associativity of Yoneda composition. This gives naturality of scalarCohomologyExtMap, hence of its AddEquiv.ofBijective wrapper scalarCohomologyExtEquiv. This argument applies also in degree zero and for zero coefficients or the empty scheme.
